title: Snake bite — keep them still and get to hospital
applies_to: Anyone bitten by a snake, or by something they did not see in grass, water, or a woodpile.

citations.source: WHO Guidelines for the Management of Snakebite Envenoming
citations.section: First aid and transport to hospital

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
WHO Regional Guidelines: Snakebite Envenoming in South-East Asia
citations.section: What not to do at the scene

steps.text: Move everyone back from where the snake is. Then look at the bite, and look at how they are breathing.
Call for an ambulance, or start arranging a vehicle now. The hospital is the treatment. Nothing you do here replaces it.
Lay them down and tell them to stay as still as they can. Moving a bitten limb pushes the venom around the body.
Take off rings, bangles, watches, and tight clothing near the bite, before the swelling starts.
Hold the bitten limb still with padding and a soft splint, and keep it level with the heart. Do not tie it tightly.
Draw a line on the skin at the edge of the swelling and write the time beside it. Do that again every 15 minutes.
Watch the eyelids, the speech, and the breathing. Drooping and slurring mean the venom is working on the nerves.
Carry them to the vehicle. Go to a hospital that keeps snake bite treatment, even if it is further away.
If the snake is already dead, photograph it from a safe distance. Never carry a live one, and never handle a dead one.

do_not: Do not cut the bite, and do not try to suck the venom out.
Do not tie a tight band or a rope around the limb. It costs people their arms and legs.
Do not put ice, herbs, paste, dung, or a hot iron on the bite.
Do not give them alcohol, and do not let them walk if you can carry them.
Do not chase the snake or try to catch it. A second bite is a real risk.
escalate_if: The eyelids droop, the speech slurs, or they cannot hold the head up — call now and say the word snake.
They stop breathing normally — start pushing on the chest and keep going.
The gums bleed, or a small cut keeps bleeding — the blood has stopped clotting.
The limb swells fast and the pain climbs — say that on the phone so treatment is ready.
They are a child, or they are pregnant — go to the hospital straight away.
